script.title: Skip the Harbour Cruise: Swap It for This in NYC

beats.narration: Your paid harbour cruise might be the weakest ticket in New York.
First-timers, one evening, normal budget. Skip the cruise. Swap in the Staten Island Ferry.
It's free, runs around the clock, about twenty-five minutes each way. Skyline, plus a distant Statue of Liberty. Cost: no commentary, and wind.
Skip the Empire State Building if you're doing Top of the Rock. That view includes it. Prices vary by date and slot, so check the official Top of the Rock site before booking sunset.
Times Square at night: keep it, ten minutes. Free. Cost: crowds.

Tell me your city and your constraint in the comments, and I'll build a plan in a future video. Links are in the description. They're affiliate links, so I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.

script.description:
A quick Skip It / Swap It for first-time New York visitors with one evening and a normal budget. The paid harbour cruise loses to a free ferry, and Top of the Rock beats the Empire State Building if you only pick one. Times Square gets a time limit, not a ban.

Disclosure: This video contains affiliate links (including GetYourGuide). I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Top of the Rock prices change by date and time slot, so check the official Top of the Rock site for current adult prices before booking.

202611171916-n2-stop-writing-just-circli.topic: Rewrite It Live: the 'just circling back' follow-up that gets ignored

script.title: Stop Writing 'Just Circling Back' (Rewrite This Instead)

beats.narration: "Just circling back" often gets no reply.
The weak version: "Just circling back on my last email." It asks for nothing, so it usually gets nothing.
Try this: "Hi Sam, I need a yes or no on the vendor quote by Thursday. If I don't hear back, I'll go with the cheaper option."
One question, one date, one default. That makes it quick to answer.
Writing to someone senior? Soften it: "Would Thursday work for a decision?" Directness varies by country and boss.
Save this script for the next time you need it, and tell me in the comments which piece of career advice I should test next.

script.description: A live rewrite of the vague 'just circling back' follow-up into a message that is easy to answer: one clear question, a date, and a default. Includes a softer version for senior people.
